source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.
prompt:
You are assisting with a scholarly experiment in structural literary analysis.

TASK: Write an ORIGINAL short prose passage in English, set in the target scenario below. It must be
a HOMEOSYNTACTIC transposition of a hidden source: hold the source's syntactic form at the level
specified below while inventing entirely new words and moving the content into the target
scenario. It is NOT a paraphrase or a translation.

FORM TARGET (hold this). Reproduce, period by period, the CLAUSE-NESTING SCHEMA below --- an indented tree in which each line is a clause (main / relative / adverbial / complement / coordinate) and indentation marks subordination (a clause indented under another is embedded in it). Hold the SAME nesting: the same clauses, each embedded under the same kind of parent clause, to the same depth. The WORD ORDER and the words themselves are entirely yours; only the clause-embedding tree is fixed.
Reproduce it for all 10 periods, in this order:
Period 1 (about 8 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
Period 2 (about 29 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - open complement (infinitive)
    - adverbial clause
Period 3 (about 3 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
Period 4 (about 15 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - relative/adnominal clause
Period 5 (about 11 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - adverbial clause
      - relative/adnominal clause
Period 6 (about 9 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - relative/adnominal clause
      - open complement (infinitive)
Period 7 (about 12 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - adverbial clause
Period 8 (about 18 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
Period 9 (about 19 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - relative/adnominal clause
      - finite complement clause
        - open complement (infinitive)
          - relative/adnominal clause
Period 10 (about 9 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - finite complement clause

TARGET SCENARIO --- render the content here (in your own words):
  - a supermarket checkout line at a busy hour
  - the conveyor belt, the barcode scanner, the bagging area, the card reader
  - the cashier and a shopper; a cart, a divider bar, a receipt
  - another shopper crowding from behind; a small friction over space in the queue
  - the register of retail routine: beeps, the total announced, loyalty-card prompts

REQUIREMENTS --- both hold together:
1. CLAUSE NESTING PRESERVED --- the same clause-embedding tree per period (which clause embeds in which, to the same depth), in any word order and words you choose.
2. COHERENT --- one continuous, fully sensible passage in the target scenario; new lexicon,
   no trace of any source content.

Write modern, natural English. Produce the 10 periods in order as continuous prose --- no
numbering, no headings. Output ONLY the passage: no preamble, no self-audit.

gens.text:
The shopper placed items swiftly on the conveyor.
Fearing delays, she wished the scanner to function flawlessly, where every beep signified success rather than a need for manual entry.
Items glided.
The divider bar separated her goods from those of the impatient customer behind.
That shopper leaned forward, nearly touching the back of her chair, whose movements grew more erratic with each passing second.
The cashier's eyes darted, noting each product before them, whose prices flickered on the screen.
Time seemed to stretch.
Her cart was nearly empty.
The card reader chimed softly, a signal to swipe, when the crowding shopper grumbled audibly, their frustration palpable.
Finally, she secured her receipt, the last tangible link to her purchases.

The cashier scanned the items swiftly.
Quickly arranging each product, hoping to ease the tension growing as more shoppers jostled behind.
The conveyor belt hummed steadily.
Every beep signaling another item tallied.
When the cart reached the divider, slowing slightly.
The shopper anxiously adjusted her stance.
Behind her, another pressed impatiently.
The card reader whirred without delay.
As the total flashed, the cashier named it clearly, prompting loyalty rewards seamlessly integrated.
A receipt printed, neatly folded for the bagging area.

The cashier scanned items briskly, the barcode reader chirping loudly.
She aimed to swiftly complete transactions, knowing every second counted when another shopper hovered impatiently behind, ready to jostle for position.
Space dwindled.
Every cartload seemed unusually heavy, laden with bulk goods.
As the conveyor belt groaned under the load, shoppers edged closer, anxious about the impending shortage of room.
The divider bar barely kept the eager second shopper at bay, their eager gaze fixed on the card reader.
When the beep signaled transaction completion, tension slightly eased.
The total was announced clearly, a robotic voice cutting through the murmurs.
A loyal customer’s card swiped smoothly, unlocking discounts for those who followed the store’s frequent shopper guidelines diligently, which often meant waiting patiently amidst the crowd.
Finally, the receipt printed, signaling closure.

The shopper pushed the cart past the divider bar into the checkout lane.
Swiftly scanning each item, the cashier aimed to clear the conveyor before another impatient customer squeezed through, hoping to expedite their purchase.
Space was tight.
Behind the glass, the barcode scanner hummed quietly, recognizing each product.
When the cashier paused, another shopper edged closer, their breath hot against the nape of her neck, the person who had waited longer now agitated.
The bagging area filled quickly as the cashier juggled bags, trying to manage the overflow that threatened to spill onto the floor.
As the total was announced, the register beeped insistently.
The loyalty-card reader lit up expectantly.
When the shopper hesitated, reaching into their wallet, the cashier gently prompted, pointing to the small screen displaying offers only available to members, the display flickering with deals tailored specifically for those who signed up.
Finally, the receipt printed, wrapping up the transaction.

The cashier tapped keys briskly, scanning items on the conveyor belt.
She aimed to process the queue swiftly, hoping the divider bar would keep another customer from crowding closer, if not for courtesy.
Space dwindled.
Every beep from the register echoed loudly, a reminder of the time ticking.
Behind her, whispers grew louder, a shopper urging the current customer to hurry, their voice tinged with impatience, someone clearly tired of waiting.
The barcode scanner paused briefly, leaving a moment's silence that stretched awkwardly, the machine searching for a signal to continue.
Meanwhile, the cashier glanced up periodically, eyeing the bagging area to ensure everything moved smoothly.
Then came the total announcement, sharp and clear, interrupting the quiet.
The customer fumbled for cards, reaching past the divider bar, where a loyalty-card prompt flashed insistently, awaiting the next step to complete their transaction.
Finally, receipts printed, signaling closure.

The clerk zapped the produce swiftly.
Gently loading groceries, they hoped to swiftly complete transactions, yet another impatient shopper loomed behind.
Time ticked.
Each beep signaled items processed, those tagged with discounts whispered savings.
Suddenly, the scanner hiccupped, scrutinizing a peculiar jam jar closely.
The loyalist card prompted urgently.
Space dwindled.
The divider creaked under pressure.
A flustered apology emerged as the cashier explained totals, another impatiently urging from behind with their cart, wishing to expedite their own checkout hastily.
The receipt printed eagerly.

The cashier swiped the first item briskly.
She aimed to pack efficiently, yet another shopper pressed from behind, impatiently nudging the divider bar with every beep of the scanner.
Items stacked.
The barcode scanner buzzed, acknowledging each product precisely.
When the total chimed, a brief murmur arose, as if the machine whispered the sum to the loyalty-card prompt beside it.
The bagger sorted meticulously, each item finding its place under the watchful eyes of the crowding shopper.
Behind the register, the conveyor belt hummed continuously.
A receipt fluttered, detailing the transaction precisely.
The shopper pondered her next move, wondering how long until the next round of purchases began, her cart already half-filled by impulse buys.

At dawn's first blush, the conveyor belt hummed.
The cashier swiped the barcode reader, eager to scan swiftly, where the crowd pressed closer.
Customers shuffled.
Behind the divider bar, whispers grew louder.
A shopper jostled from behind, when the one before hesitated.
The cart's contents spilled, which necessitated rearranging hastily.
Frustration simmered.
Through the card reader, the transaction beeped, tallying purchases aloud.
The cashier announced the total, as another shopper loomed, waiting impatiently for their turn.
She printed a receipt, showing loyalty benefits.

In the bustling aisles, the conveyor belt hummed.
The cashier scanned each item swiftly, eager to tally sums quickly, where shoppers pressed impatiently.
Items flew past.
The barcode scanner bleeped insistently.
Behind the divider, another shopper leaned forward curiously, the one whose breath whispered anxiously.
The card reader pinged loudly.
A loyal customer swiped smoothly, their fingers trembling slightly with relief.
Space narrowed as the queue jostled; tension grew.
The total flashed boldly, demanding attention, the voice prompt reminded patrons warmly of rewards pending, those who lingered hoped for quick service still.

The cashier scanned swiftly, zapping each item with precision.
She aimed to wrap up quickly, hoping to clear the line before another surge arrived, for the queue was already stretching past the divider bar.
A shopper buzzed anxiously.
Her cart jostled behind, pressing against the space between shoulders, eager to begin her own dance with the conveyer.
As the beeps chimed out each price, a murmured dispute over inches flared, the second shopper's irritation palpable as she leaned around, her voice tinged with impatience.
Her eyes darted toward the card reader, willing the transaction to complete faster.
Suddenly, the total leapt onto the screen.
A shopper lunged forward, almost touching the bagging area, to check her balance, her concern about running low evident even as she handed over her card.
Finally, the receipt spewed forth, crisp and official, detailing every purchase made, each item listed with a meticulousness that bespoke the supermarket’s pride in its records.
The loyal shopper swiped her membership card, ready to earn points for every dollar spent.
